info.name: Raise Hand API (HW4 · JWT, roles, topics & tagging)
info.description:
Live Q&A for lectures — Django REST Framework + SimpleJWT + PostgreSQL in Docker Compose.

Run the whole collection with the Runner (or newman): folder 1 registers a student and a lecturer and stores their tokens in collection variables; the lecturer token is the collection's default Bearer token, individual requests switch to the student or admin token to demonstrate 401/403; folder 3b walks through the final-project features (topics, lecture material, automatic tagging, answers, summary, export); folder 6 signs in as the demo admin and deletes the throw-away accounts.

Variables: baseUrl, demoPassword (DEMO_PASSWORD from .env, used only for the admin), the rest are filled automatically.

Docs: {{baseUrl}}/docs/ (Swagger UI with an Authorize button), docs/API.md in the repository.

item.name: Upload lecture material (JSON) → topics from headings

request.description: Lecture 1 → 1 LectureMaterial (OneToOneField). Markdown headings become topics; 'Images and layers' already exists and is updated, two topics are created. A multipart upload of a .txt/.md/.pdf file works the same way (field `file`).

body.raw:
{
  "title": "docker-lecture.md",
  "text": "# Postman demo lecture

A short lecture about Docker for the Postman run.

## Images and layers

A Dockerfile builds an image layer by layer; a changed instruction invalidates the cache of every layer below it. Keep requirements.txt before the source code so pip install stays cached.

## Networking and ports

EXPOSE documents a port; publishing happens with ports: in Compose or -p on the command line. Containers on one network reach each other by service name.

## Volumes and persistence

Named volumes survive docker compose down; down -v deletes them. Bind mounts map a host folder into the container.
"
}
